title: Built-in Baanzon Verso AI engine
highlights: A built-in AI engine (Baanzon Verso) now auto-installs, auto-starts, and powers the GUI chat with zero configuration — install, serve, and health are handled silently on first launch.
The GUI chat is fully wired to the engine with automatic gateway resolution and a no-auth fallback, so chats work out of the box.

The engine's serve path is hardened end to end: npm >= 11.4 install-scripts approval, a --no-open headless boot, and a health probe that keeps warming or provider-less engines online without restart loops.
improvements: Live Baanzon Verso engine status (installing / online / disabled / port / base URL) in the GUI provider panel.
P1 GUI polish: all 12 TUI themes ported to the GUI, theme-driven Monaco editor and xterm terminal, and a Monaco diff view.
Panel error boundaries with toast notifications and a functional run/debug panel.
Self-hosted Monaco so the GUI works without an internet connection to CDNs.
Vitest unit tests and a GUI CI job, plus guardrail ratchet maintenance across the workspace.
fixes: Engine native binaries (esbuild, @swc/core, better-sqlite3, onnxruntime-node) now actually materialize on npm >= 11.4, fixing engines that served HTTP 500s.
The health probe no longer restarts a healthy-but-warming engine or one without configured providers, while still flagging unrelated port squatters.
Release binaries no longer report stale -dev/dirty version metadata; artifacts build with accurate version strings.
jemalloc is gated to non-Windows so --all-features builds succeed on Windows.
